seo.title: Geospatial Data Sources and GIS File Support | GriidAI
seo.description: Explore verified geospatial sources, bring your own GIS data, and check upload and export formats. Connect data to reviewed analysis in GriidAI.

hero.title: Geospatial data, connected to the analysis you need.
hero.copy: Start with data you already have or work with supported geospatial sources inside GriidAI. Bring vector, raster, tabular, and multidimensional data into the workspace, review its context, and use it directly in an AI-guided spatial analysis workflow.

definition.title: What geospatial data can I use in GriidAI?
copy: GriidAI supports two data paths. You can upload supported geospatial files from your own work, or use supported external and public sources when the required access path is available. Once data is in the workspace, inspect it, select it as an input, and use it in supported analysis, mapping, and later workflow steps.

Use the source directory and format matrix on this page to check access requirements, upload and export support, and handling notes. The right input also depends on your study area, time period, variables and analytical method.

paths.title: Start with a trusted source or bring the data you already use.
paths.copy: Choose the path that fits your project. Both lead to data you can inspect in the workspace and use in a reviewed analysis.
rows: Use a supported source and narrow the request by area, time, variable or analytical need. Check the source and review the acquisition step before continuing.
Upload supported files, inspect their spatial context, and use the intended dataset in a reviewed analysis.

discovery.title: Find data in the context of the analysis.
copy: When the required source is supported, GriidAI can use the study area and analytical intent to locate or fetch relevant geospatial data, make it available in the workspace, and continue into the next analytical step.
Review the selected source, area and time coverage before continuing. Data from different sources may represent different measurements, resolutions or methods.

sequence.title: From a study area to terrain analysis.
sequence.copy: Define an area of interest, request supported elevation data, review the acquisition plan, and inspect the raster in the catalog. Use the retrieved data in a subsequent terrain step, then review the slope or aspect result.
steps: Request elevation data for the selected area.
Review the proposed source and retrieval step.
Review the terrain result before continuing.

request.copy: Make the data request specific: identify the study area, time window, variable and scale you need. Check whether the source measures observations, estimates, forecasts or modeled conditions before comparing or combining results.
request.example: Use this area of interest and the specified time window. Retrieve the required variable from a supported source, and show the source and relevant resolution before analysis.
context: Controls spatial extent and reduces unnecessary retrieval
"Use this AOI as the study area."
Avoids mixing data from the wrong period
Clarifies what the dataset must contain
30 m DEM may be suitable for regional terrain, not building engineering
Distinguishes station, satellite, reanalysis, vector mapping, etc.
Do not silently substitute scientifically different sources

byod.title: Use the data your project already depends on.
byod.copy: Upload supported geospatial data into the GriidAI workspace, organize it in the Data Catalog, inspect the map and metadata, and use the dataset as input to your next prompt or analysis step.
byod.journeyTitle: Upload once. Continue into a reviewable analysis.
steps: Choose or drop a supported dataset.
Confirm layer, map, attributes/metadata and study area.
Describe the spatial task and select the intended layer.
GriidAI proposes inputs, method, validation and expected output for supported executed steps.
User approves the step and processing runs.
Inspect map, attributes, statistics or other output context.
Export supported output or use it in the next analysis step.

plan.title: Review how your data will be used before the analysis runs.
plan.copy: When a supported step requires execution, GriidAI can present an implementation plan before the operation proceeds. The demonstrated plan structure exposes the selected inputs, method, validation approach and expected output so the user can confirm that the workflow matches the intended question.
rows: The exact uploaded layer(s) selected from workspace context.
The GIS operation or multi-step method to be applied.
Checks relevant to geometry, raster alignment, CRS, counts/statistics or stated assumptions.
The expected layer, table, raster or map-ready result.

vector.question: Which neighboring buildings fall within 50 meters of this selected property?
vector.copy: Upload building footprints, select the intended feature, and review a 50-meter buffer operation before execution. Inspect the buffer and a follow-on intersection result to identify nearby or overlapping buildings.
captions: Review the input and 50-meter buffer plan.
Check the buffer and intersection result.

output.title: Keep the result usable after the analysis.
output.copy: Inspect the result in the workspace, then export supported analytical or map outputs when the next step requires them. Check the format matrix for the available output directions and any restrictions.
output.caption: Export a supported output or continue the analysis.

sourceDirectory.title: Explore geospatial data sources
copy: Browse sources verified for use with GriidAI. See the available data types, coverage, access requirements, and related datasets or workflows. Availability can differ between products from the same provider.

Some sources are public; others require a provider account, credentials, subscription, or license. Data remains subject to the provider’s terms and availability. Check the last-verified date and the dataset details before choosing a source.

states.No filter matches: No sources match these filters. Clear a filter or bring your own data into GriidAI.
states.Unknown source: We do not currently publish a verified record for this source. Check the supported formats to bring your own data, or contact us about your requirements.
states.No approved records: Current source details are not available here yet. You can explore supported upload options below.
states.Temporary data load failure: We could not load source details. Please try again or explore the upload options below.
states.Temporary source outage: This source is temporarily unavailable through GriidAI. Check the source details for updates or use supported data you already have.

types.title: Work across the data types spatial analysis needs.
types.copy: Use feature geometries, grids, tables and multidimensional inputs where the current workflow supports them. Data type explains the structure; the format matrix below explains how files can enter and leave GriidAI.
rows: Represent discrete features with geometry and attributes.
Points, lines, polygons; buildings, roads and boundaries
Work with cell-based grids and imagery.
Elevation, land cover and satellite imagery
Use rows and fields where their meaning and relationship to the workflow are clear.
Use supported variables and slices across dimensions such as time or depth.
familyCopy: Use supported vector formats for feature-based analysis and exchange. Inspect the geometry, attributes and spatial reference before selecting a method.
Check GeoTIFF input and output support alongside its raster metadata. Resolution, bands, data type and NoData can affect the analysis and the exported result.
A table is not automatically spatial. Coordinates, identifiers related to mapped features, or a supported attribute workflow determine how its rows can be used.
Check the supported Zarr version, store structure, variables and dimensions. The selected slice and the resulting dataset must fit the downstream operation.

compatibility.title: Check your format from input to output
copy: See which formats can be uploaded, inspected, used in supported analysis, and exported. These are separate capabilities: a format accepted as an input may not be available as an output, and analysis depends on the dataset’s structure and the selected operation.
Open a format’s notes for packaging, version and handling details. Check the current status before preparing your data.
compatibility.intro: Check upload, inspection, analysis and export separately. Supported formats vary by direction, and a file that opens successfully may still need preparation before a particular operation. Use the notes beside each format for packaging, version and structure requirements.
compatibility.why: A file can be accepted by an upload path yet still have constraints that affect how it is previewed or analyzed.
states: A tabular file may be inspectable even if it is not spatial by itself.
Can be selected by relevant supported operations
Geometry, CRS, raster structure or fields may matter.
Can be produced in a stated direction

workflows.title: Use the dataset in a method you can review
workflows.copy: Data becomes useful when it stays connected to the method. Review the selected inputs, follow the supported analytical steps, inspect intermediate and final results, and continue or export when the next task requires it.
flow: Where the data originates or is accessed
The actual product/layer/collection selected for the question
The data is fetched or made available in GriidAI
The system proposes how the selected data will be used
The user checks source, CRS, resolution, time/variables and method
Map, table, analytical dataset or export becomes inspectable

relations.title: Terrain and hydrology
relations.copy: Use a compatible elevation dataset to inspect terrain and follow a published hydrology method.

relations.title: Vegetation analysis
relations.copy: Use compatible imagery and the required bands in a reviewed vegetation-index workflow.

relations.title: Coverage analysis
relations.copy: Combine facilities and relevant context to examine the coverage question defined by the method.

relations.title: Coastal screening
relations.copy: Use elevation and scenario inputs to explore coastal exposure under the stated assumptions.

workspace.title: Keep data, intermediate outputs, and analysis context in one workspace.
workspace.copy: The Data Catalog is the working inventory for a GriidAI session. Uploaded and acquired datasets can be organized, viewed on the map, inspected in tables or metadata panels, selected as prompt inputs, and carried through multi-step analysis. Intermediate analysis files can be separated from final project layers so the workspace remains understandable as the workflow grows.
workspace.inspectionTitle: Inspect the data behind the map.
workspace.inspectionCopy: Use attribute tables to examine vector records and metadata views to check the available structural and spatial information. Select the exact workspace layer for the next question so similarly named datasets do not create ambiguity.
workspace.uploadedTitle: See the data you uploaded - not just a success message.
workspace.uploadedCopy: After upload, find the dataset in the session Layers/Data Catalog. Toggle visibility, zoom to the layer where appropriate, and check whether it is vector, raster, tabular, AOI or an intermediate result.
workspace.vectorTitle: Inspect the attributes behind the geometry.
workspace.vectorCopy: For uploaded vector data, use the attribute table to inspect fields and records, make selections, and relate table records to map features.
workspace.rasterTitle: Check spatial context before running raster analysis.
workspace.rasterCopy: For raster or multidimensional inputs, safe analysis depends on more than opening the file. Resolution, dimensions, CRS, NoData behavior, valid values, time/depth dimensions and grid alignment can affect the result.
rasterContext: Distance, area and overlay assumptions depend on coordinate systems.
Controls the scale and alignment of cell-based calculations.
Prevents missing cells from being treated as measurements.
Helps validate the structure being analyzed.
Relevant for Zarr/multidimensional workflows when supported.
workspace.layerTitle: Reference the layer already in your workspace.
workspace.layerCopy: Use the layer helper to select an existing asset instead of repeatedly typing a long or ambiguous file name. This shortens prompts and reduces accidental reference to the wrong dataset when several layers have similar names.
workspace.layerCaption: Select the exact workspace layer before the plan is generated.
workspace.boundary: Workspace awareness improves input selection; it does not guarantee that the selected data is scientifically suitable for the task. The user still reviews the data and plan.

organization.title: Keep project data understandable as the analysis grows.
organization.typeFilterCopy: Use layer type filters to find vector, raster, tabular, AOI and temp/intermediate items.
organization.copy: Organize source data, intermediate results and final layers so you can follow the work. Review temporary outputs and retain the ones needed for the next step. Use layer visibility and order to manage the map without confusing that with deleting data.

readiness.title: Know what the data represents before you use it
copy: Check where the data came from, what it measures, where and when it applies, and how it is encoded. GriidAI can expose workspace metadata for inspection, while source records provide access, coverage, licensing and verification context.
Use that context to assess whether the dataset fits your question. A mapped result or an accepted upload is not a guarantee of data quality or analytical suitability.
checks: Identify the actual provider/product and applicable license or account requirement
Keep retrieval and analysis aligned with the study area
Avoid mixing periods or confusing observations with forecasts
Distinguish station observations, satellite estimates, reanalysis and other scientifically different sources
Match the dataset to the decision; regional elevation is not a building-engineering survey
Check distance, area, overlay and coordinate assumptions
Inspect fields, selections, duplicates, missing values and topology where relevant
Review alignment, dimensions, valid values, band meanings and missing-cell treatment
Indicates access/support verification; it is not the dataset’s acquisition date or update frequency
readiness.distinction: Observation date and product update frequency describe the data. Last verified describes a support/access check. CRS, structure and values shown in product metadata are different from licensing and provenance information in source records.
readiness.reviewTitle: Review your data before the analysis.
readiness.reviewCopy: Confirm the intended dataset and study area, inspect its geometry or raster structure, and check the spatial reference, units and missing-value behavior. Define any preparation needed before using the data in a reviewed method.
readiness.preparationTitle: Prepare what the analysis needs - explicitly.
preparation: Inspect the input and identify a specific problem such as duplicates, invalid naming, geometry issues or missing values.
Define the preparation action required for the task.
Review the proposed processing step where execution is needed.
Run the preparation and inspect the revised data before downstream analysis.

rooftop.title: Screening, not engineering design
rooftop.copy: Combine building footprints and a digital surface model in a reviewed rooftop-screening workflow. Check spatial overlap, CRS, resolution, dimensions and NoData before processing, then inspect building-level summaries and sanity checks. Use the results to identify buildings that may warrant closer engineering review.

technical: Distance/area/overlay results can be wrong when coordinate systems are unsuitable or mixed.
Meters/degrees/feet and attribute units can change interpretation.
Missing pixels must not silently become measurements.
A column name alone may not explain meaning, units or codes.
Inputs may be individually valid but not cover the same area.

reuse.title: Continue with trusted data instead of uploading it again.
reuse.copy: Where session data sharing is available, reuse the intended datasets in another session and continue related analysis with the same project inputs.

faq.title: Questions about using data in GriidAI

records.question: Can I use my own GIS data
records.answer: Yes, use supported file-based inputs. Check the current format record, accepted structure and applicable limits, then inspect the uploaded data before analysis.

records.question: Can GriidAI retrieve data for my study area
records.answer: For a supported source and access path, GriidAI can use the requested area and analytical context to retrieve relevant data. Check the provider’s available products and review the acquisition step.

records.question: Are all listed sources free
records.answer: No. Access may be public, account-based, credentialed or licensed, and may differ by dataset. The source record explains the relevant requirement.

records.question: What if my provider is not listed
records.answer: An absent record does not establish current GriidAI access. You can check compatible upload formats for data you already have, or contact us about the source.

records.question: Does upload support mean export support
records.answer: No. Upload, inspection, analysis and export are listed separately. Use the direction-specific matrix for the format you need.

records.question: Are Parquet and GeoParquet the same support claim
records.answer: Parquet supports tabular upload and table export. GeoParquet is available for vector export and is not listed as a direct upload format. Use the separate records for each direction.

records.question: Can I upload a ZIP archive or File Geodatabase
records.answer: Check the current record for packaging and accepted contents. ZIP is a container, and a geodatabase can contain structures with different handling requirements.

records.question: Can I use Zarr or multidimensional data
records.answer: Check the supported version, store structure, variable and dimension handling in the current Zarr record. Do not assume every store or slice is compatible.

records.question: Is uploaded data automatically cleaned
records.answer: Do not assume automatic correction. Inspect the dataset, identify the preparation required, and review supported processing steps before using the revised result.

records.question: How large can my files be
records.answer: Applicable limits can depend on the current product plan, file structure and operation. Check the approved product limits before transferring a large dataset.

records.question: Can I connect an external database
records.answer: File upload does not establish a live database connection. Check separately confirmed integration options; do not assume PostGIS, Oracle Spatial or MySQL connectivity from file support.

records.question: Can I export maps and analytical data
records.answer: Yes. Export vector data as Shapefile, GeoJSON, CSV, GeoParquet, FlatGeobuf or KML, raster data as GeoTIFF, and tables as CSV or Parquet. PNG, JPEG and PDF export the map view rather than reusable analytical data.

records.question: Can I reuse data in another session
records.answer: Where supported, session data sharing lets you reuse the intended inputs. Check the current behavior; it does not imply real-time co-editing.

records.question: Does Last verified mean the data is newly collected
records.answer: No. It records verification of the access or compatibility claim. Dataset observation dates, temporal coverage and update frequency are separate facts.

records.question: Which data providers can GriidAI use?
records.answer: Use the source directory on this page to see the current verified public inventory. Each source identifies available data categories or products, access requirements, coverage and the date its status was checked.

records.question: What GIS file formats can I use?
records.answer: Check the current matrix for upload, inspection, analysis and export support. Vector, raster, tabular, geodatabase and multidimensional paths have different requirements; ZIP packaging and map outputs are shown separately.

records.question: Can I analyze an uploaded Shapefile?
records.answer: Yes. Upload a supported Shapefile with its required companion files, inspect the layer and attributes, and select it for a supported vector operation. Review the proposed method before execution.

records.question: Can I upload and analyze a GeoTIFF?
records.answer: Yes. GeoTIFF supports upload, inspection, analysis and raster export. Inspect CRS, resolution, dimensions, bands and NoData, then select a supported raster or terrain method.

records.question: How does GriidAI use an uploaded layer?
records.answer: Select the exact layer in the workspace and describe the task. For supported executed steps, review the selected inputs, method, validation and expected output, approve execution, and inspect the result before continuing.

records.question: Does a public source require no license?
records.answer: No. Public access and licensing are different. Review the provider’s terms and the dataset-specific notes before using or redistributing data.

records.question: Will I need a provider API key?
records.answer: Some supported paths require a provider account, API key, token or subscription. The access badge explains that requirement. This website does not collect provider credentials.

records.question: How current is the source directory?
records.answer: Each public source has a Last verified date for its supported access path. Dataset collection dates and update frequency are separate. Check temporary-availability notes and dataset-specific details before relying on a source.

records.question: How are providers and datasets related?
records.answer: A provider is the source organization or service. A dataset is a particular product, collection or layer. Different datasets from one provider may have different coverage, dates and access requirements.

records.question: Does GriidAI own third-party source data?
records.answer: Third-party data remains subject to its source’s ownership, licensing and availability. GriidAI provides a supported access path and analytical context; consult the official source and dataset notes for terms.

records.question: Is this a data marketplace?
records.answer: This page explains supported data sources and how to use your own data in GriidAI. It does not offer data purchasing or selling.

records.question: What should I check before spatial analysis?
records.answer: Check source, license, study area, time period, CRS, units and the meaning of fields or variables. For raster and multidimensional inputs, also check resolution, alignment, bands, dimensions and NoData.

final.title: Start with the data your question needs
final.copy: Find a supported source or bring your own dataset. Check its context, review the method, and move into spatial analysis with GriidAI.
